t: Enosh. The grandson of Adam.
and became brutish. Became foolish.
these stars and spheres. See Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 3:1, 3:8-9.
the one who raised him and honored him. The one whom God raises and honors.
and thus say its worshippers who know its root, etc.. Those who thought that worship of the stars fulfills the will of the Creator, but did not claim that the stars themselves are the Creator.

"for among all the wise men of the nations and in all their kingdoms there is none like You," etc.. Although they recognize that there is none like You, in one thing they are regarded as brutish and foolish, in that they discipline the people to worship vanity made of wood as a means of reaching You.
and they made its image. That they made various figures (of a person or other creatures) and claimed it is the true likeness of that power (or star).
that he invented from his heart. That he fabricated.
images. Statues of the stars.
it can do good and evil. It has the ability to cause good or evil.
and the idolatrous priests. Priests of idolatry.
liars. Falsifiers.
imagine. Think in their minds.

that these images were made because of them and in their likeness. That the priests knew that the images (the statues) themselves are not gods but only a symbol of the stars and spheres, but thought that the latter are the ones who run the world.
the Rock of the worlds. God.
and in this way the world went on and proceeded. Humanity believed in these three kinds of approach to the concept of God.
when he was weaned. When he stopped nursing.
Eitan. An appellation for Abraham our forefather.
to ponder in his mind while he was small. To think about this subject while still a child.
this sphere. Which is the force that moves the course of the world (see Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 3:1).
operates constantly. It remains in force always.
and does not make anything known. A person who will acquire for him an understanding of these questions.
sunk. Immersed.
in Ur Kasdim. His city of birth.
he worshipped with them, while his heart roamed and understood. He worshipped idols with them, while in his heart he contemplated and examined the truth of the matter.
and He is the one who guides the sphere. See ibid. 1:5.
in everything that exists. In all of reality.
to answer back. To challenge.
and to argue with them. To debate with them.
the images. Idolatrous statues.

so that all the creatures who come would know Him. He informed them of the existence of the Creator and that only He should be worshipped, so that people of future generations would not continue to err as the earlier generations did.
for he prevailed over them with his proofs. That his arguments were more correct than theirs.
the king. Nimrod.
a miracle was done for him. That Nimrod threw him into a fiery furnace and the Holy One, blessed be He, saved him (see Babylonian Talmud, Pesachim 118a).
and he would walk about calling out. Proclaiming aloud the unity of God and His worship.
according to his understanding. According to his level of comprehension.
this great principle. Belief in one God and His worship.
teaches and brings back. Teaches and returns people to the way of truth.
in a study hall. A place for Torah study.
and it was made. And it was formed.
from the four elements. Fire, wind, water, earth (that is, dust; Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 3:10).
and none of all the created beings from them. For all created beings are composed of these four elements (see ibid. 4:1).
in the way that Enosh and the people of his generation worshipped at first. Who thought that the will of the Creator is that the spheres and stars be worshipped (above 1:1).
lest you wander in the eye of your heart and see. Reflect and have it occur to you.

that the Lord apportioned them to all the peoples, to be living, existing, and perishing according to the way of the world. God placed the system of the spheres in the world so that by means of them the creatures of the world exist in a cycle of existence and destruction, in the way of nature (see Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 4:3-6).
to be. So that they will be.
an intermediary. A mediator.
to be drawn after it. To be led after it.

and all these negative commandments are one matter. The warnings mentioned here ("lest you lift up," "lest he entice," "do not turn," "lest you inquire") refer to the same matter, and therefore they are counted as one negative commandment.
let us turn our minds to it. Let us turn our thought to the matter.
limited. Restricted.
clearly. In a clear manner.
what is above. From the firmament.
what is below. From the earth.
what came before. What was before the creation.
what will come after. What will be in the future.
and he does not know the measures by which to judge until he knows the truth clearly. He does not know the methods of inquiry and the proofs needed to arrive at the truth in these questions.
heresy. Denial of faith.
to remove him from the World to Come. To lose his share in the World to Come.
there are no lashes for it. For one is not flogged for a transgression unless it involves an actual act (Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:1-2).
the commandment of idolatry. The prohibition of idolatry.
equal to all the commandments together. It is equal in importance to all the commandments combined.
and from oral tradition. According to the tradition.
from Adam. The first man.
and the thought of heresy toward idolatry. That the end of the thought of heresy is to lead to idolatry.

and he is not like a Yisrael who committed a transgression punishable by stoning. Such as forbidden relations or desecration of Shabbat, for in these transgressions he does not become like a gentile in all respects.
and one who has been converted to idolatry. Who changed his religion (see Hilchot Teshuvah 3:9).

and they are never accepted as penitents. They are not treated as penitents but remain in their presumptive status, because it cannot be discerned whether their intention is pure. But if they truly repent, their repentance is accepted and they have a share in the World to Come (Responsa of the Rambam 264, and see Hilchot Teshuvah 3:14).
the essentials of the Torah. Principal matters of the Torah.
with contempt. With disdain.
with a high hand. Openly.
to converse with them. To speak with them.
and to give them any answer at all. To argue with them.
one who reviles and blasphemes. One who disgraces and curses.
both... and. They are equal in their severity and in their punishment.
therefore one hangs one who worships idols etc.. After he is stoned, he is hung on a wooden beam until shortly before sunset (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 15:6-7).
the law of the blasphemer. The law of one who curses the Name.
until he pronounces. Until he utters with his lips.
Aleph, Dalet, Nun, Yod. The "Name of lordship," which is how the Explicit Name, written Yod, Heh, Vav, Heh (the "Name of Havayah"), is pronounced (see Hilchot Tefillah 14:10).
and he blesses him. He curses him (a euphemism).
the Names that may not be erased. One of the seven names of God (see Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 6:2).
for the unique Name he is liable to stoning. If he cursed using one of the Names that may not be erased.

and for the other appellations, there is only a warning. If he cursed using one of the appellations of God, such as "Merciful" and "Gracious" (see Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 6:5), he violates a negative commandment and is not stoned (see also Hilchot Mamrim 5:2; and see further Hilchot Sanhedrin 26:3. A gentile who cursed using an appellation is liable to death - Hilchot Melachim 9:3).
and some explain that he is liable only for the Name Yod, Heh, Vav, Heh. That is, unless he cursed the Name Havayah.
both of them. Both the Name Havayah and the Name of lordship.
they examine the witnesses. They scrutinize their testimony.
with an appellation. In order to avoid mentioning the cursing of the Name explicitly.
"Yosei shall strike Yosei.". "Yosei" is an appellation for the Name of God, as both have four letters.
they send everyone outside. Except for the judges and the witnesses.
explicitly. Without an appellation.
they stand on their feet. Out of respect for the Explicit Name.
and they do not mend it. They do not rejoin the tear with a fine seam that would make it look as if it had not been torn (see Hilchot Evel 9:3).
I too heard it as he did. And he may not repeat the cursing of the Name explicitly.

within the time of a statement. The time it takes to say "Peace upon you, my teacher" (Hilchot Shevuot 2:17). Generally, a retraction within the time of a statement cancels the earlier statement, but here this rule does not apply (see also below 3:4).
it is nothing. His retraction does not help.
zealots may strike him. Those zealous for the honor of God may kill him at the time of the act (see also Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:6).
by one of the unique Names. See above, halachah 7.
even for blessing with an appellation. That he cursed with an appellation (see above, halachah 7).
one who hears from one who heard. For example, one who hears from the witnesses who heard (see above, halachah 8).
Elyakim and Shevna. Officials of King Hezekiah who heard the cursing of the Name from Rabshakeh, the Assyrian king's commander (see Isaiah 37:4).
willingly. Not under duress.
intentionally. Not inadvertently.
and forewarning. The witnesses' warning to the one committing the transgression about the gravity of his sin and its punishment.

a fixed sin offering. An offering that always comes from an animal, as opposed to the "ascending and descending" offering, which varies according to a person's financial means (see Hilchot Shegagot 1:4).
Peor. An idol of Moab.
that a person defecates before it. That he exposes himself to it and relieves himself before it.
and Markulis. A form of idol that stood at crossroads for the protection of travelers.
he clears stones away from before it. So that others can throw.
the court must know the ways of the worship. Despite the prohibition against studying the ways of idolatry (see above 2:2).
In what case does this apply?. That he is liable only when he worshiped it in its manner of worship.
shall be utterly destroyed. Shall be put to death.

sacrificing was included among the forms of worship, so why was it singled out?. In general, it is said of anyone who worships an idol that his punishment is death; why was sacrificing singled out from the general rule, so that its punishment is mentioned in a separate verse: "He who sacrifices to the gods shall be utterly destroyed."
that are used for the Name. In the service of the offerings in the Temple.
therefore it says, "You shall not bow down". The prohibition of bowing down has an additional verse to teach that one is liable for it even when it is not the idol's manner of worship.
and the same applies to one who burns incense or pours a libation. These belong to the service of the offerings in the Temple, and are derived from sacrificing.
and throwing and pouring a libation are the same. Throwing blood and pouring wine have the same law.
he threw. He threw excrement into its mouth or onto it.
chamber pot. A vessel designated for urine.
he is liable. Because these resemble throwing and pouring.
if he slaughtered a locust for it, he is exempt. Since slaughtering a locust is not considered sacrificing at all.

if he slaughtered an animal lacking a limb for it, he is exempt. Since its slaughter is not considered the prohibited sacrificing, as it is not the way of gentiles to offer such an animal to an idol (below 9:6).
if he broke a staff before it, he is liable. Since its manner of worship is with a staff.
and it becomes forbidden. The staff becomes forbidden, like an animal slaughtered as an idolatrous offering (see below 8:1).
for the staff remains as it was. And therefore throwing it is not considered an act done to the staff (see there).
one who accepts upon himself any of the kinds of idols. That it has already been made an idol.
even if he lifted a brick. That has not yet been made an idol.
he is liable. Since by this he made it an idol (see below 8:3).
and even if he retracted within the time of a statement. See above 2:9.
in a manner of disgrace. That he intended to disgrace it.
for his inadvertence. Because he thought the matter was permitted.
who desired a form. A desire arose in him to worship it.
because of its craftsmanship. The way the image was made.
they imagine. They mistakenly think.
by one of the four services. See above, halachah 2.
one who hugs. Embraces.
and one who sweeps. Cleans.
and one who sprinkles. Sprinkles water on the dust so it does not rise.
and one who anoints. Anoints with oil and the like.
violates a negative commandment, as it says, "and you shall not serve them". Although this is not its manner of worship, there is a prohibition against honoring it with these acts.

he is not flogged for any of them, since they are not explicit. Rather, they are included in the general prohibition "you shall not serve them," and therefore one is not flogged for them, by the law of a "prohibition of generalities" (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:3).
he shall bow down. He shall bend over.
spouts that spray water in front of an idol. An idol made in the form of a face from which water emerges.
even though he did not make it with his own hand. Rather, through a craftsman who made it for him.
you shall not make for yourself. From here we learn the prohibition against making an image for oneself, even if he does not make it with his own hands.
you shall not make for yourselves. From here we learn that the very making of an image is forbidden even if he does not make it for himself.
he is flogged twice. Because of "you shall not make for yourself" and because of "you shall not make for yourselves."
the painting and the carving in a palace. Splendid halls whose walls are customarily decorated with plaster designs or carved with protruding forms.
sunken. Recessed inward.
pigments. Colors.
these are permitted. Because they do not protrude. [Note: The word "noy" is written and vocalized by the Rambam in his Commentary on the Mishnah as "no'i."]
a seal. A signet.
it is forbidden to place it. On one's finger, out of concern that it may be mistaken as being for idolatry.
and it is permitted to stamp with it. Because it creates a sunken form.
and even on a tablet. Where the form is not protruding, it is forbidden.
those who lead astray a city of Israel. Who persuaded and led the people of the city to worship idols.
even though they themselves did not worship. The instigators themselves.
but they led astray the residents of their city until they worshiped it. But if the people of the city did not worship it, the instigators are exempt.
are killed by the sword. Beheading with a blade (Hilchot Sanhedrin 15:4; and see also there 14:1).

it shall not be heard from your mouth. "And you shall not mention the name of other gods; it shall not be heard from your mouth," and from here we learn the prohibition against causing another to worship idols.
men went out. The minimum of the plural is two.
from your midst. From the same tribe.
and until they lead astray the majority of it. The majority of the city.
they judge it as individuals. And an individual who worshiped idols is punished by stoning (above 3:1).
or if a minority of it was led astray. Of a city.
who were led astray on their own. They led themselves astray.
from outside it. And not from the people of the city or the tribe.
and their property goes to their heirs. Their property passes to their heirs, unlike the property of the people of a condemned city, which is entirely burned (below, halachah 6).
like the rest of those executed by the court. See also Hilchot Mamrim 7:14.
the Great Court of seventy-one. The Great Sanhedrin, called the Great Court, which sits in the Chamber of Hewn Stone in the Temple (Hilchot Sanhedrin 1:3).
in the court of each and every gate. The lesser Sanhedrin of twenty-three judges, which sits at the entrance of each city (there), and where most capital cases are judged (Hilchot Sanhedrin 5:2).
of the cities of refuge. Cities to which one who killed inadvertently goes into exile (Hilchot Rotze'ach 5:1).
in one of your cities. A city set aside as a city of refuge is not called "your city" because it does not belong to any one person.
because it was not divided among the tribes. Rather, it belongs to all of Israel and is not called "your city."
on the border. A city located at the frontier.
so that gentiles will not enter. Through the destroyed city.
let us go and worship. Any idolatry whatsoever in its manner of worship.
of the four services. Sacrificing, burning incense, pouring libations, and bowing down (above 3:3).
when it is fit to become a condemned city. When the conditions detailed above are met in it.
if they repent, good. And they are not judged as a condemned city, but as individuals who worshiped idols.
but if they persist in their folly. Their foolishness, and continue to worship idols.
they lay siege to them. They make a siege around the city.
until the city is breached. Until they break into it.
they separate him. Until it is clarified whether a majority or a minority was led astray.
children and women. For they too are killed together with the men who were led astray.
its spoil. Its property.
its public square. The place where the townspeople gather.
until it is brought into it. That the wall surrounds the square.
every living soul in it. That even the animals in the city are killed.
with the city. With the houses of the city.
since they dwelt there. And therefore their property is included in the property of the city.
in any amount. Even slight benefit.
he receives one set of lashes. He is punished with lashes for one negative commandment, unlike one who benefits from an idol, who receives two sets (see below 7:2).
whose witnesses were proven to be conspiring witnesses. Whose testimony was refuted by other witnesses.
acquires. The property.
and it is permitted to benefit from it, since they were proven false. And it is not considered the spoil of a condemned city.
he declared his property ownerless. He despaired of holding on to his property.
a caravan. Passersby.
if he stayed there thirty days. The length of time after which they are considered residents of the city (see Hilchot Nedarim 9:17).
are killed by the sword and their property is lost. Like the other residents of the condemned city.
they are stoned and their property goes to their heirs. By the law of individuals who worship idols.
another city. A different town.
even though they took responsibility upon themselves. To pay their value if they are lost, they are nevertheless not considered the city's property.
if they were gathered with it. If they were brought into the city before its spoil was burned.
half of it belonging to the condemned city and half to another city. An animal owned by two partners, one of whom lives in the condemned city and the other outside it.
it is forbidden. And it cannot be slaughtered and divided, because the half of the animal belonging to the resident of the condemned city is subject to death, and slaughter has no effect on it.
that was slaughtered. After the sentence of burning was decreed upon the city.
like a stoned ox that was slaughtered. Which is forbidden for benefit (Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 4:22).
the hair of the head... is permitted for benefit. Since it is not included in the body (see Hilchot Evel 14:21).
and the same applies to the hair of the head. For it too is lacking detachment from the head.
consecrated items. Animals or property that were consecrated to the Temple.
offering-sanctified items. Animals fit for sacrifice.
shall die. And they are not killed by hand like the other animals of the city that are not included in "its spoil" (for the way they are put to death, compare Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin 4:1).
the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination. And therefore they cannot be offered, nor redeemed with their proceeds used to bring an offering.
items sanctified for the Temple's upkeep. Property consecrated for the needs of the Temple.
shall be redeemed. With money that is given to the Temple treasury.
its spoil and not the spoil of Heaven. And therefore they should not be burned before they are redeemed.
the firstborn and the tithe. The firstborn animal and the animal tithe.
unblemished. Without a blemish and fit for sacrifice.
and blemished ones are included in its animals. For once a blemish has befallen them, they are considered the kohen's property (see Hilchot Bekhorot 1:3).
and they are killed. Together with the rest of the animals of the condemned city.
if they came into the hands of a kohen, they shall rot. And they are not burned by hand because of the sanctity of terumah (see Hilchot Terumot 12:1).
sanctity of the body. They have inherent sanctity, and cannot be redeemed.

second tithe and second-tithe money. The tithe separated after the first tithe, which is eaten in Jerusalem, or the money with which it is redeemed (see Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni 2:1-2), and they are not burned because of their sanctity.
one who entices an Israelite. To worship idols.
whether a man or a woman. Who was enticed.
a commoner. An ordinary person.
this one is a misleader. And his law differs from that of the enticer, for the misleader is liable only when those led astray worshiped the idol (above 4:1).
and those led astray are like individuals. Who are stoned and whose property goes to their heirs (see above 4:5).

and if the majority of the city was led astray after him, he is stoned. But if the majority of the people of the city were not led astray, his death is by strangulation, like a false prophet (see below, halachah 6, and Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 9:5).
with a certain service that is the way that idol is worshiped. For one is liable for idolatry only when he worships it in its manner of worship (see above 3:2).
I will sacrifice etc.. And these acts are forbidden with regard to every kind of idol (see above 3:3).
and the enticer does not require forewarning. Unlike the other prohibitions in the Torah, for which one is not punished without forewarning (Hilchot Sanhedrin 12:1-2, 15:4; and see also there 11:5).
if he said to one etc.. Since a single person cannot testify alone, the one being enticed deceives him so that there will be two witnesses to the enticement.
to hide for him. To conceal witnesses who will lie in wait for the enticer, as detailed below.
in private. Alone.
those standing there at a distance. The hidden witnesses.
to kill him. Himself.

and because it says of one who hates you, "you shall surely release it with him". The Torah's command to a person to help load and unload a burden from a donkey even if it belongs to his enemy, and to leave his hatred aside (Targum Onkelos there, and see above in the list of commandments, positive commandment 15).
you shall not stand by the blood of your neighbor. The Torah's command to save an Israelite from mortal danger (Hilchot Rotze'ach 1:14).
and a warning to a commoner who entices. To an ordinary person who entices; the warning regarding a prophet who entices is explained below.
even if they accepted it from him and said to him "yes," he is not stoned. Because they intended to mock him and not to worship.
yes. Yes.
and was willing. Agreed, even before he worshiped.
he stated the halachah correctly. He stated the correct halachah.
and that prophet shall die. Any death stated in the Torah without specification is death by strangulation (Hilchot Sanhedrin 14:1).
to argue and debate. To dispute.
and one does not ask him for a sign and a wonder. Unlike a true prophet, whom it is permitted to test by having him state things that are going to happen (Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 10:1).
and he neither added nor subtracted. From the commandments of the Torah and their laws.
he goes in the ways of prophecy. He conducts himself as a prophet (see Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 7:4).
you shall not fear. Do not be afraid.
and likewise one who swears by it to a gentile. Who swears by the name of an idol so that the gentile will believe him.
by its object of fear. By his idol.
wait for me. Wait for me.
in the sacred writings. In Scripture.
Peor. An idol of Moab (see Numbers 25:3).
and Bel and Nevo. Idols of Babylon (see Isaiah 46:1).
and Gad. Also an idol (see Isaiah 65:11).
willingly. Not under duress.
intentionally. Not inadvertently.

a fixed sin offering. An offering that always comes from an animal, as opposed to the "ascending and descending" offering, which varies according to a person's financial means (see Hilchot Shegagot 1:4).
and waves it. Moves it back and forth.
in a whisper. Softly.
until the questioner hears as if one were speaking with him. The person who comes to the necromancer to inquire of the ov imagines that he is conversing with the person who was raised by the ov.
and as if it is not noticeable to the ear but he senses it in thought. It is not an actual voice but imagination.
and divines with it. Whispers incantations toward it.
from under his armpit. From beneath the armpit.
very low. A low voice.
a bird whose name is known. The name of the bird is known (Commentary on the Mishnah, Sanhedrin 7:7).
until he falls like an epileptic. Like a person suffering from the falling sickness (epilepsy).
and where is the warning for them?. The warning not to do these acts.

"and of your seed you shall not give to pass to Molech... there shall not be found among you one who makes his son or daughter pass through fire". That he is not liable until he does both: gives to Molech and passes through fire (see below, halachah 4).
part of his seed. Some of his children and not all (see below, halachah 4).
to the priests, the fire worshipers. The priests of this idol, who worship fire.
they give the son to his father. They return him to his father.
with their permission. By their giving permission.

and he passes him by his foot from one side to the other through the flame. The son walks on his own feet and his father pulls him by the hand and passes him quickly from one side of the fire to the other without his being burned.

one who does this service for another idol besides Molech is exempt. For this passing through fire is not defined as the burning of incense that is prohibited for every idol (see above 3:3), since the son is not burned.
and he caused him to pass not in the manner of passing. That the son did not walk on his own feet, for example if the father carried his son in his arms.
a disqualified seed. One born from a forbidden union.
blind. Sightless.
asleep or blind, he is exempt. Since he cannot pass on his own feet independently, it is considered not in the manner of passing.
a figured stone. A stone with a design that was placed before an idol to bow down upon (see also Sefer HaMitzvot, negative commandment 12).
in the other lands. And even in the Land of Israel, outside the Temple site.
the cut stones. Stones that are cut and hewn (see Hilchot Beit HaBechirah 1:8).
and because of this. Because of this prohibition.
all of Israel have the custom of spreading mats in synagogues paved with stones. See Hilchot Tefillah 11:5.
paved. Floored with stone.
goes to another place. That has no stone floor.
or bends on his side and tilts. Bows on his side and tilts his head sideways (see Hilchot Tefillah 5:14).
one who bows to the Lord... without spreading out hands and feet. With his face to the ground.
lashes for rebelliousness. Lashes by rabbinic decree.
beside. Next to.
a barren tree. One that does not produce edible fruit.
porticoes. A roofed structure made of wood.
all the porticoes... that were in the Temple were of stone, not of wood. See also Hilchot Beit HaBechirah 1:9.
to destroy idolatry and its accessories. To obliterate and annihilate it and the utensils with which it is served (for the manner of destruction see below 8:6).

you shall utterly destroy all the places. The continuation of the verse: "where the nations served... and you shall tear down their altars and smash their pillars and burn their Asherim with fire and cut down the images of their gods and destroy their name from that place."
to pursue it. To search for it in all its places in order to destroy it.
rather, every place that is conquered etc.. Only in places outside the Land conquered by Israel must one search for idolatry and destroy it.
from that place. From the Land of Israel.
and its accessories. The utensils with which it is served.
and its offerings. Objects given to it as an offering or gift (see below, halachot 15-16).
is forbidden for benefit. That no useful benefit may be derived from it.
and nothing of the devoted property shall cling to your hand. Said regarding the spoil of a condemned city, which was forbidden as devoted property because of the gravity of idolatry (see above 4:7).

even its dung and its bones etc.. Although they are not part of its flesh (see for example Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 4:18, Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTumot 1:7), because all of it is included in the offering to the idol (see also Hilchot Ishut 5:2).
for example, if they used to do etc.. That they used to do so for the sake of an idolatrous offering.
and likewise anything similar. That anything whose connection to idolatry is known by a sign is forbidden for benefit.
is forbidden for benefit immediately. After it was made.
from when he carved it. From the time the gentile made it into an idol.

and sets it in secret. "Cursed be the man who makes a graven or molten image, an abomination to the Lord, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it in secret," and from here they learned that it is not forbidden until he "sets it in secret."
things done in secret that are its service. That an Israelite does not want others to know that he worships it, and he worships only in secret.
and accessories of idolatry. Utensils or other objects used for the cult.
are not forbidden until they are used. That the use is what causes them to be forbidden.
for others. Not for his own use.
for he is flogged. Because of the prohibition "and you shall not make for yourselves molten gods" (above 3:9).
his wages are permitted. And they are not considered payment for an idol, which is forbidden for benefit (below, halachah 9, Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 13:15).
and even if he made it for a gentile, for whom it is forbidden immediately. By the law of a gentile who makes an idol for himself, his wages are nevertheless permitted.
because it is not forbidden until it is finished. The prohibition of benefit applies only upon completion of the work of making the image.
and the last blow. The craftsman's final action, which completes the creation.
it is not worth a perutah. It has no monetary value. Thus the payment was given for work done before the time of the prohibition.
one who buys scrap. One who buys broken metal vessels.
if he gave money and did not pull. He did not perform the act of acquisition by pulling the scrap.
he returns them to the gentile. He cancels the sale, and is not obligated to destroy them since he did not acquire them.
even though pulling by a gentile acquires. Compare Hilchot Zechiyah UMatanah 1:14.
it is like a mistaken purchase. Therefore, although the idol came into his hand, it is not considered to be in his possession and he is not obligated to destroy it.
if he pulled and gave money, he takes it to the Dead Sea. For in this case the idol is considered to be in his possession and he is obligated to destroy it.
once they came into the possession of the convert, they are forbidden. And he must destroy them (see also Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 13:22-23).
for ornament. As decoration.
the images found in the villages. Whose people are not accustomed to deal in ornamentation.
in the city. In the town.
at the entrance of the city. Which is a sign of importance.
the form of a staff or a bird etc.. Objects symbolizing authority.
a crown. A diadem.
images. Human figures.
in the markets. Public places.
these are permitted. Since their being thrown away is a sign that they are not idols.
and needless to say, fragments of images. Which certainly should be presumed not to be idols (and see below 8:11 for the law of fragments of idols).

since he knew for certain etc.. In a case of clear knowledge that it is an idol, one may not permit its whole limbs unless it has been nullified (for the law of nullification by a gentile see below 8:8).
and on other vessels. That are not honored vessels.

and a dragon. A human figure with fins and many scales on its back (Commentary on the Mishnah, Avodah Zarah 3:3). In the opinion of many commentators it refers to a creature resembling a snake with protrusions on its body, or at least on its neck (see Babylonian Talmud, Avodah Zarah 43a and Rashi there).
they forbid in any amount. If they became mixed with permitted things, everything becomes forbidden for benefit.
a cup of idolatry. An example of accessories of idolatry.
a piece of meat etc.. An example of an idolatrous offering (below, halachah 15).
a hide torn at the heart. Which is torn opposite the heart with a round tear, and is presumed to have been offered to an idol (above, halachah 3).
he transgressed and sold an idol. Even though it is forbidden for benefit.
the proceeds are forbidden for benefit. The prohibition takes hold even of the money received in exchange (unlike other prohibitions of benefit - see Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 8:16, 13:15).
its ashes are forbidden for benefit. For this too is benefit from an idol.
but the flame is permitted. One may light from the fire itself.
in a storehouse. A warehouse.
one cup separated from the mixture. One of the cups left, from among those cups with which a cup of idolatry had become mixed.

and fell among a second set of cups, they are permitted. For there is a double doubt ("safek sefeika"): the first mixture became forbidden only out of doubt, whether it was an idolatrous cup, and one of these cups then became mixed with others, which is a further doubt.
and two of them fell into the Great Sea. And were completely lost.
for I say that ring was among the two that fell. Since the rings that fell are completely lost, we assume that the prohibition was in them.

if it was mixed with a hundred and they were divided... for I say that the forbidden ring is among the majority. Since all the rings exist, the prohibition is certainly among them, and therefore we follow the majority.
the Asherah. A tree used for idolatry.
that was worshiped. That the tree itself was worshiped.
it is forbidden to sit in the shade of its trunk. In the shade of the trunk, for this is a kind of benefit from idolatry.
in the shade of the branches. The thin branches, whose shade is not significant.
passes under it while running. To show that his going there is not by his wish.
chicks that nested in it. Found in a nest on the Asherah.
and they do not need their mother. They are independent.
and the nest itself. The branches from which it is made.
brings its wood from elsewhere. And it is not from the wood of the Asherah.
took wood from it. Took wood from the Asherah for fuel.
it shall be left to cool. One must wait until the oven cools, so as not to benefit from the heat of the Asherah's wood.
the bread is forbidden for benefit. That was baked from the heat of the Asherah's wood (see Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 16:22).
and the other loaves are permitted. Since the prohibition itself is not noticeable in the bread, they were lenient regarding mixtures, unlike a mixture with actual idolatry (above, halachah 9).
took from it a weaver's rod. Took from the Asherah a stick to make into a weaving implement.
both in the summer days, when they need shade. Even in summer, when the shade of the Asherah helps them grow.
these vegetables are caused to grow. Both together cause it, not the prohibited thing alone (see also Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni 10:21).
therefore a field that he fertilized etc.. For even in these cases the forbidden and the permitted cause the growth together.
that they prepared to offer them. They designated them for this, but have not yet offered them directly before it.
and everything found in an idolatrous temple... is forbidden for benefit. For it is presumed to have been offered to it.
garments. Clothing.
in a manner of disgrace. Placed in a way that is not honorable, and it is evident that they are not an offering.
in a manner of honor. Where it appears that they were placed there to adorn the idol.
a vessel inverted over its head. Upside down, with the idol's head in the cavity of the vessel.
for something of its kind is offered on the altar. That something of its type is offered in the Temple.
it is forbidden. Because of the offering.
In what case does this apply?. That there is a difference between a manner of honor and a manner of disgrace, and between things that are offered on the altar and those that are not.
and Peor and Markulis. Whose accepted manner of worship is in a manner of disgrace (above 3:2).
that had a bathhouse or a garden. Owned by it.
one may benefit from them without gratitude etc.. It is permitted to use them, provided one does not feel gratitude toward the idol.
it had it together with others. A partnership in the bathhouse or garden.
in gratitude to the priests etc.. Since the place is jointly owned, feeling gratitude toward the priests does not look like strengthening the hands of idolatry.
provided he does not pay rent. For then he would be benefiting the idol.
a bathhouse that has an idol in it. In which an idol image stands.
standing over the drain, and everyone urinates before it. For this is the custom in a bathhouse.
and if this was its manner of worship, it is forbidden to enter it. For then they treat it as divine according to its manner of worship (see above 3:2).
it is permitted because he is damaging it. That he killed an animal, and thus there is no benefit from idolatry here.

an animal in danger of dying... because he is repairing it. One that is about to die from illness, which people hurry to slaughter to make it fit to eat before it dies and becomes forbidden as a carcass (see Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 4:11-15).
he cut it in a manner of loss and destruction. In a way that damages the meat.
anything that has no human handiwork. That was not altered by human hands.
that was designated for idolatry. That it was set aside for this.
whether they designated it to be worshiped. That it was prepared for idolatry so that it would itself be an idol.
or whether they designated it to be offered. That it would serve as an offering to an idol.
as long as he did not perform an act upon it. A significant change to the animal's body.
that he slaughtered a siman of it. The windpipe or the gullet.
made it an exchange for an idol. He exchanged an idol for it.
that became like the proceeds of an idol. They are forbidden like it (above 7:9).
for a person cannot forbid something that is not his. One cannot apply a prohibition to what is not one's property (see also Hilchot Shechitah 2:21).
to the ground of the world. The soil of the earth.
he dug pits in it... forbade it. For this ground has human handiwork.
that the wave uprooted. And that were torn from the sea.
he took them in his hand. And therefore they have human handiwork.
mountain stones that had come loose. That were detached from their connection by themselves.
and worshiped them in their place. Without their having been moved to another place.
who stood a brick upright. He set a brick upright, to make it an idol.
and a gentile came and bowed to it, he forbids it for benefit. For an Israelite's idol becomes forbidden only if it was worshiped, and its mere preparation for this is not enough (above 7:4).

for standing it up is an act. Since this action prepares the brick for idolatry, another person who worshiped it can also forbid it; otherwise a person cannot forbid something that is not his (above, halachah 2).
stood up an egg etc.. That the act of standing it up is effective to make it considered handled by people.
cut a gourd etc.. And the cutting makes it considered handled by people.
attached to it. Partly connected.
like a hand to the half that is worshiped. It is considered secondary to the worshiped half, and becomes forbidden because of it.

and this is the Asherah mentioned in the Torah. The one mentioned in the Torah as a tree of idolatry, whose law is cutting down and burning. This applies only where it was planted from the start to be worshiped; but if it was planted for fruit and was later worshiped, it is not forbidden, since it has no human handiwork (above, halachah 1).
and trimmed it and shaped it. Cut from it to improve and beautify it.
layered it and grafted it onto the trunk of a tree. Acts that are a sort of planting of branches of the tree itself.
and sprouted shoots. New branches.
he cuts down the shoots... and the rest of the tree is permitted. Only the parts that were altered for the sake of idolatry became forbidden because of that.
although its body was not forbidden. For a planted tree has no human handiwork (above, halachah 1).
that are prepared to make beer etc.. Those fruits are intended for making the drink.
because by default it is an Asherah. It should be assumed by default that it is an Asherah.
for this is the practice of an Asherah. For this is how they treated Asherah trees.
as long as it is under it, it is forbidden for benefit. For it serves the idol.
because the tree itself is not what is worshiped. And therefore even its produce was not forbidden.
a house that the gentile built from the start so that the house itself would be worshiped. And it becomes forbidden immediately, by the law of an idol made by a gentile (above 7:4).
and likewise one who bows to a built house. For it was made by human hands.
and plastered it and decorated it. They renovated it with plaster and craftsmanship.
he removes what he added. He removes it from the house.
and shaped it and decorated it so that it would be worshiped. That they improved it so that it would be made an idol.
in the body of the stone. That he did not add to it, but carved into it.
if he removed the idol, the stone is permitted. For the stone itself is not what is worshiped.
adjacent to an idolatrous temple. Close to the boundary of the temple.
it is forbidden to build it. For it turns out to be a cause of benefit to the idol, in that they could use the wall that reaches its boundary.
he moves in into his own. Into his own area, and builds at some distance from the idolatrous temple.
so as not to extend etc.. So that the idol will not benefit from the additional area.
if the wall belonged to him and to the idol. If it was a wall jointly owned by both of them, and it fell.
it is divided half and half. The wall's materials are divided between the two, and only the part belonging to the idol is forbidden for benefit.
its stones, its wood, and its dust. Of an idolatrous temple that fell (see Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTumot 6:5).
grinds. Grinds fine.
and scatters to the wind. Disperses the material so that the wind carries it away.
and casts into the Dead Sea. To a place where the material will be lost and will not be of use (and the Dead Sea is the Great Sea - Hilchot Arachin VaCharamin 8:8, according to accurate versions).

its coverings are forbidden for benefit. The materials with which these objects are adorned. For these worshiped objects are considered idols for every purpose, apart from the prohibition on their body.
that gentiles nullified. They disqualified it and desecrated it from being an idol.
and they treat them as divine. The law of destruction applies only to images that are treated as gods.

an Israelite's idol is never nullified... and requires burial. For it is forbidden because it was worshiped and not because of its making (above 7:4); therefore its law is stricter, that it cannot be nullified, but on the other hand there is no commandment to destroy its body like a gentile's idol, rather it is buried intact.
that came into the hands of an Israelite. And became his property.
his nullification does not help at all. For the law of destruction applies to it from the moment it came into the hands of an Israelite.
and an Israelite does not nullify an idol. For he has no role in the matter of idolatry.
even in the gentile's domain. Even while the idol is still with the gentile.
a minor gentile or a fool etc.. For in order to nullify an idol, the gentile must understand the nature of his act.
whom an Israelite forced. Compelled him to nullify it.
but one who does not worship, his nullification is not nullification. For he too does not understand the nature of idolatry.
if he nullified its accessories. Since they are secondary to it. And if the idol itself is nullified, its accessories are nullified as well.

and an idolatrous offering is never nullified. For Scripture calls the offering "sacrifices of the dead," and it is expounded that it is like a corpse, which is forbidden for benefit and has no permitted state (see Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTumot 6:7).
he flattened its face. He flattened part of its face with a blow.
that he did not diminish it. He did not cut off any of the body of the idol.
he sold it to an Israelite goldsmith. It is clear to the selling gentile that the goldsmith will melt it, and did not buy it for worship.
but if he pawned it... it is not nullified. For all these acts are reversible, and therefore are interpreted as an expression of temporary anger and not as nullification.
that its worshipers abandoned. They left it and abandoned it.
in a time of peace. When there was no factor forcing them to abandon it, it is reasonable that they left it because they no longer worship it and have nullified it.
that broke by itself. It fell apart without people breaking it.
one who finds fragments of an idol etc.. It is uncertain whether it was nullified or broke by itself, and we are stringent as long as it is not known that they nullified it (see also above 7:7).
that is made of sections. Composed of pieces that fit together.
and a commoner can reassemble it. No expert is needed to put it together.
he must nullify each and every section. For each section has importance by itself.
and if he cannot reassemble it etc.. The sections have no importance on their own, only as part of the whole.
an altar of idolatry. Which is among the accessories of idolatry, forbidden for benefit (above 7:2).
until most of it is torn down by gentiles. And then they certainly nullified it from its use.
and a bimos. A stone on which an idol is set.
and a bimos that was damaged is permitted. Once it is damaged it is not used for this, and no nullification is needed (Ma'aseh HaMelech; and see above, halachah 5).
the stones of Markulis. Whose worship is by throwing stones (above 3:2).
that he built a structure with them etc.. The gentile used them for practical purposes, which proves that he nullified them.
he trimmed etc.. He cut off parts of it for his use.
that he smoothed. He planed and removed parts of it.
not for its needs. Not for the benefit of the tree's growth, but because he needed those parts.
and its trimmings are permitted. For they were nullified from being idolatry once they were cut from the Asherah.
and if it belonged to an Israelite etc.. As above, halachah 9.
their festivals. A term of mourning, and it is a euphemism for the day of their festival (see Commentary on the Mishnah, Avodah Zarah 1:1).
to take. To buy.
it is forbidden to take from them etc.. All these are forbidden because they cause profit or benefit to the gentile, who then goes and gives thanks to his idol on his festival day.
and to sell them something that lasts. Something that is preserved until their festival.
a loan by document or against a pledge. Because of the document or pledge there is no concern that the Jew's money will not be repaid.
because it is like saving it from their hands. For there is a concern that they will not repay.
until the day of their festival. But not on the day of their festival itself.
in the Land of Israel. Where the attitude toward idolatry is stricter (see above 7:1).
a gift. A present.
he feared enmity. The hatred that would result from his refusal.
on all their festivals. On all the days of their festival.
and they praise. They extol.
a private festival. A personal holiday.
that he came up from the sea. Returned from a sea voyage.
that it is known that there is idolatry in it. And it is considered a festival day by those who practice it.
designated for a certain kind of idolatry. That offerings or incense of those things are made to it.
it is forbidden to sell them to the worshipers of that idol. Because it strengthens their hands in idolatry (below, halachah 8).
unspecified. When the gentile did not state explicitly that they are for idolatry.
one does not sell them anything that can cause harm to the public. So as not to help them corrupt the world (see Commentary on the Mishnah, Avodah Zarah 1:7).
and weapons. Instruments of war.
to an Israelite robber. A Jewish bandit, because this strengthens the hands of transgressors (see also Hilchot Rotze'ach 12:12-14).
when the road is exclusive to that place. And there is no other route to reach his destination, so it is forbidden because he benefits from passage through this city.
and it happened. It came to him by chance.
permitted. Since he has the option of going another way, and there is no complete benefit here.
a dome. A rounded building.
decorated. Adorned.
because it benefits the idol. Through the rent payment.
its proceeds are permitted. For he benefited from it against his will.

and writes and records in their registries. He writes a bill of sale and gives it validity in a gentile court in order to save his money, although it is generally forbidden to litigate in their courts (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 26:7).
and flutes of idolatry. Wind instruments used in eulogies.
one may go to a gentile fair. One held not on their festival and not in a city where there is idolatry.
and slaves and maidservants while still gentiles. While they are still gentiles.
and writes and records in their registries because it is like saving it from their hands. So that they will not contest the sale.
the merchant. The trader.
he severs its hooves from the knee down. He tears off its hooves so that no benefit can be derived from it.

they neither raise nor lower. If he is in mortal danger, we do not rescue him (for example by lifting him out of a pit), but we also do not put him into such danger (see Hilchot Arachin VaCharamin 8:9).

and even for the Israelite to eat and drink his own there is forbidden. Although there is no concern of gentile cooking (see Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 17:9). [Note: The Rambam in the Commentary on the Mishnah vocalizes the word "me'eimatai" as "me'ammatai."]
it is because of idolatry. Out of concern of drawing close to idolatry.
she delivers for pay because of enmity. Out of concern that hatred will arise.
under her supervision. Under the supervision of the Israelite woman.
so that she will not kill it. For gentiles are suspected of bloodshed (see Hilchot Rotze'ach 12:7).
to a tarfut. A despised and loathsome thing, a term for idolatrous temples where they celebrate (see Commentary on the Mishnah, Avodah Zarah 2:3).
it is forbidden to do business with them. Just as it is forbidden to do business with them before their festivals (above, halachah 1).
provided they are not bound to one another. That they do not travel together in a caravan, but as individuals.
lest he change his mind. And not go to the tarfut.
and on the return it is forbidden. Lest he sold an idol there, and its proceeds are forbidden (see the next halachah).
an apostate Israelite, both on the way there and on the way back, it is forbidden. On the way there, because he might not return; on the way back, because of the proceeds of idolatry in his hand.
to a gentile fair. Where there is idolatry.
and the proceeds of idolatry in the hand of an Israelite are forbidden for benefit. For it takes hold of its proceeds, as it says, "and you shall be devoted like it" (above 7:9).
and in the hand of a gentile they are permitted. For the teaching above was said regarding an Israelite only, and not gentiles.
so that we make peace with them and leave them to worship it. In such a way that they live with us in peace and continue to worship idols (see also Hilchot Melachim 8:9).
if one saw a gentile worshiping idols who is lost or drowning in the river, he should not lift him out etc.. See also Hilchot Rotze'ach 4:11.
informers of Israel. One who hands over his fellow or his fellow's property to gentiles (Hilchot Teshuvah 3:12).
and the minim and the apikorsim. These terms here refer to all who deny the fundamental principles of faith (see Hilchot Teshuvah 3:7-8).

it is a commandment to destroy them with the hand and to lower them to the well of destruction. And it is permitted to kill them even without witnesses and judges, even at a time when capital cases are not judged (Hilchot Chovel UMazik 8:10, Hilchot Mamrim 3:2; and see also Hilchot Edut 11:10).
from here you learn. From the fact that there is a prohibition against saving them.
and a resident alien. For its definition see below, halachah 6.
since you are commanded to sustain him. As it says, "a stranger and a resident, and he shall live with you" (Leviticus 25:35; and see also Hilchot Shabbat 2:12).

and in Syria. The lands David conquered outside the land of Canaan, whose status is greater than that of the Diaspora but not at the level of the Land of Israel (Hilchot Terumot 1:3; for details of its borders see there 1:9).
exempts it from the tithes. For when the field is in the hands of the gentile, he sows it and does not separate tithes.
houses to make them a storehouse. To be used for storage.

he sells once he cuts or sells it to him on condition to cut, and he cuts. They may be sold only after he cut them from the ground, or if he sold them on condition that he cut them after the transaction.
but he may give to a resident alien. For there is a commandment to sustain him, as above, halachah 2 (and see also Hilchot Zechiyah UMatanah 3:11).

we sustain the poor of the gentiles along with the poor of Israel for the sake of the ways of peace. See also Hilchot Matnot Aniyim 7:7, Hilchot Melachim 10:12; for further laws for the sake of the ways of peace see Hilchot Evel 14:12.

and we do not protest the hands of the gentile poor etc.. We do not stop them when they take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field, even though these are meant for the poor of Israel (see also Hilchot Matnot Aniyim 1:9).
even on the day of their festival. It is permitted to greet an idol worshiper, provided that he does not greet him in a way that makes it appear that the Jew rejoices with him in his festival.
and one never doubles the greeting to them. Saying "peace, peace" to an idol worshiper is forbidden at any time.
he greets him with a soft voice and a bowed head. For a similar law see Hilchot Ta'aniyot 3:8, 5:11.

all these things are not said etc.. The prohibitions of lo tichanem detailed above, which limit relations between Israel and the nations, apply only where there are neighborly relations between them. But when the hand of Israel is strong, such relations do not exist at all, because of the prohibition "they shall not dwell in your land."
as it says, "they shall not dwell in your land". "Lest they cause you to sin against Me."

and if he accepted upon himself the seven commandments, he is a resident alien. He is called so because it is permitted to settle him in the Land of Israel (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 14:7; for the process of his acceptance see Hilchot Melachim 10:10-11).

and a resident alien is accepted only when the Jubilee is in effect. When all the inhabitants are on the Land, and each tribe dwells in its place. Since the exile of the two and a half tribes the Jubilee years have ceased and a resident alien is not accepted (Hilchot Shemitah VeYovel 10:8-9; and see also Hilchot Milah 1:6, Hilchot Shabbat 20:14, Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 14:8).
a righteous convert. A gentile who converts and accepts all the commandments of the Torah (for the process of his conversion see there 14:1-6).
in the statutes of the nations. The customs of the gentiles.
be drawn. Be led on.
in his knowledge and in his opinions. In his beliefs and in his conduct.
and he shall not grow a forelock like the forelock of their heads. He shall not grow his hair like them, and perhaps it means that he shall not braid it in the way they do.
and he shall not shave the hair from in front of his face etc.. He shall not shave all his hair in front and leave hair only at the back of the head.
three fingers on every side. A distance of three fingerbreadths in every direction.
he withdraws his hand. He stops cutting his hair, so as not to help grow the gentile's forelock.
may meet me. May happen upon me.
that crowed in the evening. At night
,. Unlike the usual crowing of roosters, which is in the morning.

like Eliezer, servant of Abraham. Who set himself a sign that the girl of whom he would ask for water, and who would offer him a drink and also water his camels, would be the one he would take as a wife for Isaac (Genesis 24:12-14).
that he become quiet and his thoughts be cleared. That he reach a mental state in which he thinks of nothing else.
who bends to the ground. Lies down on the ground.
a lantern. A lamp.
and they imagine and say. They speak by the power of imagination.
lashes for rebelliousness. Lashes by rabbinic decree.
is flogged. By Torah law.
those who set the times. Those who determine which season suits each thing.
who say by astrology. Who observe the stars and say.
and anyone who does an act... at the time that the astrologers set. Planned to do his deeds at the time the stargazers recommended for him.
one who deceives the eyes etc.. Performs an act in a way that misleads onlookers into thinking he did something wondrous.
this is included in "one who practices divination". For this too is learned from the term "me'onen."
with words that are not in a human language and have no meaning. Meaningless words.
and even on Shabbat. And there is no prohibition of idle speech on Shabbat in this (see Hilchot Shabbat 24:4).
so that his mind does not become confused. So that he does not go mad and his condition worsen.
a psalm from Psalms. From the Book of Psalms.
it is forbidden to consult a necromancer or a diviner. The acts of the ov and the yidoni were explained above, 6:1-2.
one who deceives the eyes etc.. Performs an act that misleads onlookers into thinking it is an act of sorcery.

is flogged with lashes for rebelliousness, because this prohibition stated regarding the sorcerer etc.. Since he did not perform an actual act of sorcery, he is not stoned. And although he violates the prohibition of "there shall not be found among you," he is not flogged for it because the essence of the prohibition relates to the death penalty and not to lashes (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:2).
that they incline after them. That they lean toward their ways.
benefit. Usefulness.
corners of. Sides of.
his temples. The sides of the head.
and a kohen shall not defile himself for the dead. The prohibition for a kohen to become impure to a corpse; the daughters of kohanim were not warned against this (see Hilchot Evel 3:11).
from time to time and not constant. A commandment whose obligation is not constant but depends on certain times.
except for kiddush of the day. On the nights of Shabbat and festivals (see Hilchot Shabbat 29:1, 29:18).
and eating matzah on the nights of Passover. Hilchot Chametz UMatzah 6:10.
and eating the Passover offering. Eating the Passover offering on the night of the fifteenth of Nisan (Hilchot Korban Pesach 8:1).
and its slaughter. There, 1:1.
and Hakhel. The commandment that all of Israel assemble at the Temple on the Sukkot festival following the Shemitah year (for its details see Hilchot Chagigah chapter 3).
and rejoicing. Bringing peace offerings of rejoicing on the three pilgrimage festivals (see there 1:1).
a tumtum. One whose sexual organs are covered and it is not discernible whether he is male or female. [Note: The Rambam in the Commentary on the Mishnah vocalizes this word "tumtom."]
and an androginos. One who has both male and female sexual organs.
are in doubt. Whether their law is that of a man or a woman (see Hilchot Ishut 2:24-25).
and the Sages did not set a measure for this pe'ah that is left at the temple. The Sages did not fix the width of the pe'ah that it is forbidden to shave.
to pluck. To cut.
a razor. A knife.
and there are five pe'ot in it. There are five parts of the beard where shaving is prohibited.
and the shibolet of the beard. The hair on the chin.
a woman shall not adorn herself with the adornment of a man. She shall not adorn herself with a man's ornaments.
or shave her head like a man. Similar to a man's haircut.
and jewelry. An ornament.
because he adorned himself with a woman's adornment etc.. For it is the way of women to darken and pluck the white hairs from their heads.
he does not wrap himself like a woman. He does not wrap himself in women's garments.
kohl. Black dye.
other lasting dyes. Other colors that remain.
that they mark themselves for their idolatry etc.. They make a mark on their bodies as a sign that they are bound to it.
and tattoos. He fills the place of the incision with color.

both Israelite and kohen. They are flogged for this prohibition, and a kohen is not flogged for an additional prohibition of "nor shall they make any cuttings in their flesh" (Leviticus 21:5), which was stated to kohanim.
gedidah and seritah are one. Seritah is with the hand and gedidah with an instrument, and both are forbidden for the dead.
